candidates.speaker: Eric Hernandez
candidates.proposition: The existence of evil presupposes objective morality and natural teleology, both of which require God and therefore undermine atheism.
candidates.attributionBasis: The moderator explicitly introduces Eric, and this uninterrupted opening statement follows that introduction until the applause and speaker change.
candidates.loadBearingReason: This is the first of Eric's three announced arguments and directly converts a standard objection to God into affirmative evidence for theism.
candidates.contextSummary: Eric argues that evil requires an objective moral standard and a proper-function teleology that atheistic naturalism cannot ground, whereas God can ground both.

candidates.speaker: Eric Hernandez
candidates.proposition: Atheistic evolution supplies an undercutting defeater for cognitive reliability because natural selection favors adaptive behavior rather than truth.
candidates.attributionBasis: The material remains within Eric's uninterrupted opening statement and is explicitly announced as his second argument.
candidates.loadBearingReason: The cognitive-reliability argument is one of the three principal pillars of Eric's cumulative case and is presented as making atheism epistemically self-defeating.
candidates.contextSummary: Eric contends that undesigned faculties selected for survival need not produce true beliefs, so naturalism defeats justification for atheism and knowledge generally.

candidates.speaker: Eric Hernandez
candidates.proposition: Consciousness and libertarian free will require an immaterial soul, while naturalism permits only physical causes and therefore cannot accommodate either.
candidates.attributionBasis: Eric explicitly labels this his final argument, and the same uninterrupted statement continues through his conclusion and the subsequent applause.
candidates.loadBearingReason: This is the third announced pillar of Eric's case, linking consciousness, agency, moral responsibility, and rational belief directly to theism.
candidates.contextSummary: Eric uses differences between mental and physical properties plus causal closure to argue that consciousness and free agency require a soul unavailable on naturalism.

candidates.speaker: Justin Schieber
candidates.proposition: Naturalism has an initial explanatory advantage over theism because it posits fewer fundamental kinds of entities, powers, agents, and causal relations.
candidates.attributionBasis: Justin begins immediately after Eric's concluding applause, identifies his naturalist position, and delivers an uninterrupted opening statement.
candidates.loadBearingReason: Qualitative simplicity supplies the comparative framework through which Justin asks the audience to weigh all three of his evidential arguments.
candidates.contextSummary: Justin defines naturalism as one basic kind of scientifically governed stuff and argues that theism bears extra ontological commitments without an initial offsetting benefit.

candidates.speaker: Justin Schieber
candidates.proposition: The scale and character of evolutionary animal suffering are more probable on morally indifferent naturalism than under a compassionate, omnipotent creator.
candidates.attributionBasis: Justin explicitly announces this as his first item of evidence during his uninterrupted opening case for naturalism.
candidates.loadBearingReason: Evolutionary suffering is one of Justin's three principal comparative arguments and directly bears on whether naturalism or theism better explains evil.
candidates.contextSummary: Justin contrasts naturalism's expectation of fragile embodied organisms and unconstrained evolution with God's freedom to create life without predation and prolonged animal misery.

candidates.speaker: Justin Schieber
candidates.proposition: The universe's near-total hostility to embodied moral agents is expected on indifferent naturalism but surprising under a rational creator oriented toward value.
candidates.attributionBasis: Justin marks this as his second piece of evidence, and it occurs within his continuous opening statement without any speaker interruption.
candidates.loadBearingReason: Cosmic hostility is one of Justin's three headline facts and provides a direct comparative inference favoring naturalism over value-oriented theism.
candidates.contextSummary: Justin argues that naturalism predicts rare life-permitting regions, whereas a value-oriented creator should make more of the physical world compatible with embodied moral agency.

candidates.speaker: Justin Schieber
candidates.proposition: The existence and unequal distribution of nonresistant nonbelief are surprising if God is perfectly loving but readily explained by natural cultural transmission.
candidates.attributionBasis: Justin announces his final evidence as nonresistant nonbelief, and the argument continues uninterrupted through its conclusion in the supplied lookahead.
candidates.loadBearingReason: Divine hiddenness is Justin's third principal comparative argument and directly tests the relational expectations generated by perfect divine love.
candidates.contextSummary: Justin argues that perfect love would provide willing people sufficient grounds for relationship, yet sincere unbelief varies geographically and historically like an ordinary cultural belief.
